patterns.name: Shell command built from a variable
patterns.message: A shell command is assembled from data instead of a fixed argument list, so anything that reaches it can run arbitrary commands.
patterns.suggestion: Pass arguments as a list (spawn/execFile with an argv array) instead of building one command string.

patterns.name: Subprocess with shell=True
patterns.message: shell=True hands the command to a shell, so any interpolated value becomes shell syntax.
patterns.suggestion: Use shell=False with an argument list; if a shell really is required, validate the input against an allowlist first.

patterns.name: Dynamic code evaluation
patterns.message: eval / new Function execute a string as code: any input that reaches it is arbitrary code execution.
patterns.suggestion: Parse the data instead (JSON.parse, a template engine, a lookup table) rather than evaluating it.

patterns.name: Piping a download into a shell
patterns.message: Piping a remote response into a shell executes whatever the server returns at that moment; the bytes are never reviewed and can change between runs.
patterns.suggestion: Download to a file, verify its checksum or signature, then run it.

patterns.name: TLS certificate verification disabled
patterns.message: Verification is turned off, so the connection accepts any certificate — this is a man-in-the-middle opening, not a workaround for a broken test host.
patterns.suggestion: Fix the trust chain (add the CA to the trust store) instead of disabling verification.

patterns.name: SQL assembled from strings
patterns.message: A query is built by concatenation or interpolation, so the caller controls the SQL.
patterns.suggestion: Use parameterised queries / prepared statements and pass values as bind parameters.

patterns.name: SQL assembled with a format string
patterns.message: The query text is formatted with the values baked in, which is string interpolation by another name.
patterns.suggestion: Pass the values as parameters: cursor.execute(sql, params).

patterns.name: Assigning to innerHTML
patterns.message: Writing markup into the DOM executes scripts embedded in it if any part of the string is attacker-controlled.
patterns.suggestion: Set textContent, or build DOM nodes; if markup is genuinely required, sanitise it with a maintained library first.

patterns.name: Filesystem path built from request data
patterns.message: A path is derived from request data, so callers can escape the intended directory with ../ or an absolute path.
patterns.suggestion: Resolve the path and verify it is inside the expected root (path.relative / realpath prefix check) before touching it.

patterns.name: Deserialising untrusted data
patterns.message: Some deserialisers can construct arbitrary objects and run code while doing so; parsing attacker-supplied bytes with them is remote code execution.
patterns.suggestion: Use a data-only format (JSON, TOML) or the safe variant (yaml.safe_load).

patterns.name: Hardcoded credential
patterns.message: A credential is committed in the source. Once it is in the repository it is in every clone and every history rewrite is somebody's weekend.
patterns.suggestion: Read it from the environment or a secret store, and rotate the exposed value.

patterns.name: Non-cryptographic randomness for a security value
patterns.message: Math.random / time are predictable; anything that must not be guessable needs a CSPRNG.
patterns.suggestion: Use crypto.randomUUID / crypto.randomBytes (or secrets.token_hex) and give it enough entropy.

patterns.name: Password hashed with a fast digest
patterns.message: md5/sha1 are fast and unsalted: password hashes built with them fall to a wordlist in seconds.
patterns.suggestion: Use a password hash: bcrypt, scrypt or argon2.

patterns.name: Authorization check disabled
patterns.message: A security check is switched off in code. This is the change reviewers most often miss, because it looks like configuration.
patterns.suggestion: Keep the check and fix what it rejects; if it must be off, scope it to a named test and make that explicit.

patterns.name: Wildcard CORS together with credentials
patterns.message: Any origin may send credentialed requests, which lets any site act as the logged-in user.
patterns.suggestion: Echo back an allowlisted origin instead of *, and keep credentials scoped to it.

patterns.name: Debug mode or stack traces exposed
patterns.message: Debug mode and raw tracebacks leak source, configuration and sometimes state to whoever triggers the error.
patterns.suggestion: Gate it behind an environment check that is off by default, and log the trace instead of returning it.

patterns.name: Session cookie without HttpOnly/Secure
patterns.message: A session cookie without HttpOnly can be read by any script on the page, and without Secure it travels in clear text.
patterns.suggestion: Set httpOnly, secure and sameSite on every session cookie.

patterns.name: JWT signature not verified
patterns.message: Decoding without verifying the signature accepts a token anyone can forge.
patterns.suggestion: Always pass the expected algorithms and verify against the signing key.

patterns.name: World-writable file permissions
patterns.message: World-readable (and often world-writable) permissions expose the file to every local user.
patterns.suggestion: Use the narrowest mode that works — 0600 for secrets and credentials.

patterns.name: Request to a caller-supplied URL
patterns.message: The server fetches a URL the caller chose, which reaches internal services and cloud metadata endpoints.
patterns.suggestion: Validate the host against an allowlist and block private/link-local ranges before issuing the request.

patterns.name: Untrusted event data interpolated into a workflow step
patterns.message: An issue title, PR body or commit message interpolated straight into `run:` is attacker-controlled shell input — the classic GitHub Actions workflow injection.
patterns.suggestion: Put the value in an `env:` entry (env: TITLE: ${{ github.event.issue.title }}) and reference it as "$TITLE" in run:, instead of interpolating ${{ }} into the command.

patterns.name: torch.load without weights_only
patterns.message: torch.load defaults to weights_only=False, which unpickles arbitrary objects and therefore runs arbitrary code from the file.
patterns.suggestion: Pass weights_only=True when the file holds only tensors and plain data (or set TORCH_FORCE_WEIGHTS_ONLY_LOAD=1).

patterns.name: Python stdlib XML parser
patterns.message: The stdlib XML parsers resolve external entities by default, so untrusted XML can read local files (XXE) or exhaust memory (billion laughs).
patterns.suggestion: Parse with defusedxml.ElementTree, or explicitly disable entity resolution before parsing.

patterns.name: crypto.createCipher (no IV)
patterns.message: createCipher derives the key with a weak KDF and takes no IV, so the same plaintext always encrypts the same way. It was removed in Node 22.
patterns.suggestion: Use crypto.createCipheriv() / createDecipheriv() with a random IV and an authenticated mode such as GCM.

patterns.name: AES in ECB mode
patterns.message: ECB encrypts each block independently, so identical plaintext blocks produce identical ciphertext and the structure of the data leaks.
patterns.suggestion: Use AES-GCM, or AES-CBC with a random IV plus an HMAC over the ciphertext.

patterns.name: External script without Subresource Integrity
patterns.message: A remote script tag with no integrity attribute executes whatever the CDN or the network hands back, so a compromised origin runs code in your page.
patterns.suggestion: Add integrity="sha384-…" crossorigin="anonymous" to the tag, or self-host the script.

patterns.name: insertAdjacentHTML with dynamic content
patterns.message: insertAdjacentHTML parses its argument as HTML, so any caller-supplied string in it is an XSS sink.
patterns.suggestion: Use insertAdjacentText() when the content is text, or sanitize with DOMPurify before inserting HTML.

patterns.name: Go exec.Command through a shell
patterns.message: Invoking a shell and building its command line by concatenation lets anything in the arguments be interpreted as shell syntax.
patterns.suggestion: Call the program directly with an argument list (exec.Command("ping", "-c", "1", host)) instead of going through sh -c.
